newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Number of options open to Wellworths-Fitzwilton.
newsitem.headline: Number of options open to Wellworths-Fitzwilton.

text.p: Fitzwilton Plc said on Thursday that there were a number of options facing its Northern Irish food retailer, Wellworths, including a possible move into the Republic of Ireland and the creation of a potential all-island retailing company.
"They also include co-venturing with other companies whose size and buying power make them attractive to us," Fitzwilton chairman Tony O'Reilly said in a results statement.
Earlier, the industrial holding company announced 1996 pre-tax profits of 15.11 million punts against 15.03 million a year earlier.
It said operating profits at Wellworth totalled 18.8 million sterling, down seven percent on 1995, while sales rose by six percent to 291 million.
The retail chain now has a market share of around 17.5 percent in Northern Ireland, Fitzwilton said.
"Wellworth is now entering a new era, an era of change, an era of competition and paradoxically, an era of increased opportunity."

"Wellworths, with 60 years experience in the province, in good times and bad, has, we believe, the capacity to take on allcomers and to invest heavily in new stores and new formats that, as with Superquinn in the south, will be appealing to the consumer," Fitzwilton said.

Developing and extending product choice and quality are key elements of Wellworths' plans, while higher margins in the non-food range has been a major differentiating factor between Wellworth and its main competitors, Fitzwilton said.
Wellworths has developed its leisure and entertainment range and is now a retailer of videos, CDs and books where it sees good growth opportunties.

It has also ensured that it has the long-term finance available to acquire new sites and develop them in a manner consistent with the competition by issuing 80 million sterling of bonds due 2006, Fitzwilton said.

To date, it has acquired three prime sites in Northern Ireland, all with the benefit of planning permission for food retailing, and has committed over 18 million stg. The sites will be developed over the next year.
